ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Settled at Tell es-Sultan from about 9000 BCE beside its springs, one of the oldest continuously inhabited places in the world.
The largest city in the world in the fourth millennium BCE, where temple administrators began recording goods on clay tablets around 3300 BCE.
Founded around 3100 BCE where the Nile valley meets the Delta, Egypt's capital for much of its history, with the pyramids of the Old Kingdom in its cemeteries.
For over a thousand years it controlled river traffic on the middle Euphrates; its archive of some 20,000 tablets survived Hammurabi's conquest.
Platform mounds and sunken circular plazas from about 2600 BCE make it one of the oldest cities in the Americas.
Planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, linked by sea through the Gulf to Mesopotamia, whose texts probably call the land Meluhha.
Capital of the Third Dynasty of Ur, whose kings raised its great ziggurat, until the Elamites sacked it around 2004 BCE.
The last Shang capital, near Anyang: palace and temple foundations, royal tombs, bronze workshops and tens of thousands of inscribed oracle bones.
A planned city of perhaps 100,000 people in the Valley of Mexico, among the largest in the world in the 3rd to 6th centuries CE.
